q: Exercise 1. Put these letters in their Abgad order: ܓ , ܐ , ܒ
opts: Right: Alaph, Beth, Gamal begin the alphabet.
That reverses the order; Alaph comes first.

q: Exercise 1. Put these letters in their Abgad order: ܝ , ܚ , ܛ
opts: Right: Ḥeth, Ṭeth, Yodh are letters 8–10.

q: Exercise 1. Put these letters in their Abgad order: ܪ , ܩ , ܫ
opts: Right: Qoph, Resh, Shin are letters 19–21.
Shin is the second-to-last letter, after Resh.

q: Exercise 2. In ܢܘܗܪܐ (nūhrā, “light”), which letters are non-joiners (they do not connect to the letter on their left)?
opts: Right: all four stop the cursive connection to the left.
He (ܗ) and Alaph (ܐ) are also non-joiners.
explain: The Syriac non-joiners are ܐ ܕ ܗ ܘ ܙ ܨ ܪ ܬ.

q: Exercise 3. Write M-L-K-A (“king”) in Syriac letters.
opts: The first letter should be Mim (ܡ), not Nun (ܢ).

q: Exercise 3. Write A-L-H-A (“God”) in Syriac letters.
opts: The third letter is He (ܗ), not Ḥeth (ܚ).

q: Exercise 3. Write Y-W-Ḥ-N-N (Yukhannan, “John”) in Syriac letters.
opts: The third letter is Ḥeth (ܚ), not He (ܗ).
There are two Nuns at the end.
That is the right letters in the wrong order; Syriac is written right to left starting with Yodh.

q: Exercise 4. Reading ܐܠܗܐ, which letter do you read first?
opts: The letter on the far right (ܐ, Alaph)
Right: Syriac runs right to left.
The letter on the far left
That is the last letter; Syriac runs right to left.
Order depends on direction, not height.
He is the third letter read.
